text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, is often asymptomatic, meaning it does not cause noticeable symptoms. However, there are some signs that may indicate high blood pressure, including:

list.snippet: Headaches: Especially in the morning or after physical activity
Fatigue: Feeling tired or lacking energy
Shortness of breath: During everyday activities
Chest pain or discomfort: (in severe cases)

text_blocks.snippet: To accurately determine if you have high blood pressure, it is essential to get your blood pressure checked by a healthcare professional. They will use a blood pressure monitor to measure your systolic (top number) and diastolic (bottom number) pressures. A normal blood pressure reading is below 120/80 mmHg. High blood pressure is diagnosed when your readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mmHg.

If you experience any of the symptoms listed above, it is important to consult a healthcare professional for evaluation. Early detection and treatment of high blood pressure can help prevent serious health complications such as heart disease, stroke, and kidney failure.
